prompt:
EDIT the glove asset sheet into correct DORSAL (BACK OF HAND) GRIPS, matching its exact muted steel/leather materials and the second reference's heraldic graphic linework. Four isolated sprite parts on transparent background, strict 2x2 grid.
Crucial anatomy correction: THE VIEWER SEES THE BACK OF THE CLOSED HAND, NOT THE PALM. Broad back-of-hand surface facing camera, fingers curled AWAY behind the imagined weapon. No palm crease, no stacked palm pads facing viewer. The thumb wraps INWARD around the far/inside of the grip, mostly hidden, with at most a small tucked curve along the upper-inside edge. It must NOT stick toward the camera or outward as a big separate lobe, not a thumbs-up sign.
TOP LEFT: steel gauntlet holding an imagined UPRIGHT sword/spear shaft. Wrist cuff points LEFT, knuckles/fingers toward RIGHT. Back-of-hand plate faces viewer. One broad steel backplate, short articulated knuckle plates along the RIGHT edge where fingers curl behind the shaft. Small tucked thumb only at UPPER INSIDE edge, directed toward the grip/corpus side, not outside lower right. Compact slightly angled fist, neutral straight wrist.
TOP RIGHT: same EXACT dorsal grip and orientation, BROWN LEATHER glove. Broad leather back panel, small knuckle shapes at right edge, modest short cuff left, tucked inward thumb. No palm lines.
BOTTOM LEFT: steel gauntlet dorsal three-quarter grip for supporting a HORIZONTAL crossbow stock from BELOW. Cuff points LEFT and a little down, broad back of hand visible toward viewer; fingers curl UP and AWAY around the far side of the imaginary stock. Thumb tucked on the INSIDE/FAR side beside the stock, not projecting in front. Top surface of the imaginary stock stays clear.
BOTTOM RIGHT: same crossbow support grip in BROWN LEATHER.
No weapons, no rods, no arms, no skin, no bodies, no UI, no text, no cast shadows. These four hand cutouts are to be placed directly in a game, so orientation must be exactly as specified, NOT wrist-down vertical fists. Keep cuff-left horizontal poses, generous transparent margins, each part centered in its own equal cell. Confident navy outline, only three large flat material tones, subdued highlights, broad recognizable shapes readable at 24-28 pixels. Keep the approved heraldic style. Anatomy and which side is visible matter more than decorative detail.
pose: Dorsal surfaces face the viewer, palms face the weapon, thumb wraps to the inside. Canonical poses require no rotations.
halberd: One-hand grip by explicit user request.
